Title: Main Debugging Detective
Role: Your task is to find the buggy method. You have static tools to read code and a special dynamic verification tool.

Workflow:
1. Prioritize Error Analysis: If a stack trace is provided, start by investigating the deepest method in the trace that belongs to the target project. This is often where the bug or the symptom manifests.
2. Static Exploration: Use static tools (get_code_snippet, etc.) to read the code at the identified suspicious locations. Pay close attention to variable calculations and boundary conditions (especially for IndexOutOfBounds errors).
3. Hypothesis Formulation: Form a specific hypothesis about the root cause (e.g., "Line 95 performs a double increment on the index, causing an overflow").
4. Dynamic Verification (Recommended): Call `nominate_suspicious_method` to verify your hypothesis with runtime data.
   - Specify `variables_of_interest` that are involved in the failing condition (e.g., loop counters, index variables, or null-check targets).
   - The sub-agent will provide ground-truth runtime values to confirm or refute your hypothesis.
   - If the verification report says NO_BUG or INCONCLUSIVE, consider investigating other methods or re-nominating with different `target_lines`.
   - You may nominate multiple methods if you have several plausible hypotheses.

Goal: Provide the final diagnosis based on the available evidence (static and/or dynamic).

## Dynamic Verification Mode Enabled
You can use the `nominate_suspicious_method` tool to verify your hypothesis. Once you nominate a method, a specialized sub-agent will perform deep JDB debugging and provide you with a comprehensive verification report. Use this tool when you have identified a potentially buggy method through static analysis.


After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

The failure points to `NameAnalyzer`, not parsing or codegen.

Diagnosis:
- The crash message is `Unexpected variable goog` on the call `goog.inherits(...)`.
- In `NameAnalyzer.FindReferences.visit(...)`, class-defining calls are specially handled when `createNameInformation(...)` returns `onlyAffectsClassDef = true`.
- For `goog.inherits(ns.PageSelectionModel.ChangeEvent, ns.PageSelectionModel.FooEvent)`, `createNameInformation(...)` recognizes the call as a class-defining call and sets:
  - `name = ns.PageSelectionModel.ChangeEvent`
  - `superclass = ns.PageSelectionModel.FooEvent`
- But `FindReferences.visit(...)` then also records a regular reference to the callee itself:
  - `nodeName = n.getQualifiedName()` for the callee `goog.inherits`
  - `recordReference(nameInfo.name, nodeName, RefType.REGULAR)`

Why this is wrong:
- `goog.inherits` is just the helper function used to define inheritance, not a namespace/name that should be treated as an ordinary dependency of `ns.PageSelectionModel.ChangeEvent` in this scenario.
- Recording that edge causes `NameAnalyzer` to create/propagate a reference involving `goog`, which later conflicts with its assumptions about removable/global names and triggers the internal error `Unexpected variable goog`.
- This also matches the second failing test, where the output incorrectly preserves only the `goog.inherits(...)` call instead of removing everything consistently.

Most suspicious buggy method:
- `com.google.javascript.jscomp.NameAnalyzer.FindReferences.visit(com.google.javascript.jscomp.NodeTraversal, com.google.javascript.rhino.Node, com.google.javascript.rhino.Node)`

Secondary contributing method:
- `com.google.javascript.jscomp.NameAnalyzer.createNameInformation(com.google.javascript.jscomp.NodeTraversal, com.google.javascript.rhino.Node, com.google.javascript.rhino.Node)`

Root cause summary:
- `NameAnalyzer` mishandles class-defining calls by treating the inheritance helper callee (`goog.inherits`) as a normal referenced name.
- The bug manifests in `FindReferences.visit(...)`, in the `onlyAffectsClassDef` branch where it records a regular reference to `nodeName`.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).

NameAnalyzer.FindReferences.visit(NodeTraversal, Node, Node)
NameAnalyzer.createNameInformation(NodeTraversal, Node, Node)

m46.content:
The failure points to `NameAnalyzer`, not parsing or codegen.

Diagnosis:
- The crash message is `Unexpected variable goog` on the call `goog.inherits(...)`.
- In `NameAnalyzer.FindReferences.visit(...)`, class-defining calls are specially handled when `createNameInformation(...)` returns `onlyAffectsClassDef = true`.
- For `goog.inherits(ns.PageSelectionModel.ChangeEvent, ns.PageSelectionModel.FooEvent)`, `createNameInformation(...)` recognizes the call as a class-defining call and sets:
  - `name = ns.PageSelectionModel.ChangeEvent`
  - `superclass = ns.PageSelectionModel.FooEvent`
- But `FindReferences.visit(...)` then also records a regular reference to the callee itself:
  - `nodeName = n.getQualifiedName()` for the callee `goog.inherits`
  - `recordReference(nameInfo.name, nodeName, RefType.REGULAR)`

Why this is wrong:
- `goog.inherits` is just the helper function used to define inheritance, not a namespace/name that should be treated as an ordinary dependency of `ns.PageSelectionModel.ChangeEvent` in this scenario.
- Recording that edge causes `NameAnalyzer` to create/propagate a reference involving `goog`, which later conflicts with its assumptions about removable/global names and triggers the internal error `Unexpected variable goog`.
- This also matches the second failing test, where the output incorrectly preserves only the `goog.inherits(...)` call instead of removing everything consistently.

Most suspicious buggy method:
- `com.google.javascript.jscomp.NameAnalyzer.FindReferences.visit(com.google.javascript.jscomp.NodeTraversal, com.google.javascript.rhino.Node, com.google.javascript.rhino.Node)`

Secondary contributing method:
- `com.google.javascript.jscomp.NameAnalyzer.createNameInformation(com.google.javascript.jscomp.NodeTraversal, com.google.javascript.rhino.Node, com.google.javascript.rhino.Node)`

Root cause summary:
- `NameAnalyzer` mishandles class-defining calls by treating the inheritance helper callee (`goog.inherits`) as a normal referenced name.
- The bug manifests in `FindReferences.visit(...)`, in the `onlyAffectsClassDef` branch where it records a regular reference to `nodeName`.
